There is a tiny bar section, and a table right at the entrance of the restaurant that will fit a maximum of 5 people. There aren't really any servers, and the waiter/waitress takes your order over the bar area. The sushi is delicious and so impeccably made. Everything tasted so fresh, and when I asked for extra masago on the side, they obliged! They also have really unique rolls, one which includes strips of mango on the top. This type of creativity makes me want to go back again and again to try out new rolls. I recommend this place to anyone who likes take-out, doesn't mind small spaces, and can tolerate a possible lack of service. Fantastic food!

text: So I guess all of these great reviews are for the $10 lunch buffet. Let's talk about dinner shall we? A year and a half ago my husband and I won a $100 gift certificate for this place at a fundraising event. It was clearly marked "No Exp." We're huge fans of Ekta, so when we have a hankering for Indian, we usually go there. But we were in the neighborhood last night and thought, what the heck? We were surprised to see the restaurant nearly empty. Only three other tables were seated. We enter the restaurant and stand near the host station. We wait for a few minutes as servers continue to walk around us. No one stops to say, "We'll be right with you." It's was like we were invisible. We said, "If it weren't for the gift card, we'd walk right out the door." After about five minutes we made it very apparent that we wanted a seat. I actually had to FLAG someone down. In an EMPTY restaurant, why on earth were we being ignored as we waited by the host station? Then, rather than sit us by a window, they sat us at a oddly placed table in a thoroughfare, in the back of the restaurant. Now, the place is nearly empty - why wouldn't they put patrons in the nicer seats by the windows? If anything it would make the restaurant look slightly less dead. It was 8:45PM at night - it's not like they were going to get a dinner rush at that point. Whatever. So we were finally seated about seven minutes after entering the establishment with NO apology. Nothing. I think a "Sorry for the wait" would have been in order. So we order our meal and some wine. Again, in an empty restaurant, the wine takes ten minutes to get to the table. I could have walked home and grabbed a bottle in that amount of time. We began to think, "No wonder this place is so empty." Food: I almost considered giving Palace two stars because the Naan was legit and we enjoyed the Lamb Saag. But the prices were ridiculous considering the poor service. (Again, apparently they have a cheap lunch buffet...) Each main dish was around $22-25. At Ekta, where the food blows this place out of the water, each main is $10 cheaper. In a restaurant with $20+ courses, you'd expect a more professional vibe from the staff. We were gobsmacked by the prices, and while the food was good, it was no Ekta. And at that price point, we'd never come back (without a gift certificate!) But what we experienced after we ate, pretty much sealed the deal. We hand our waiter the gift card and he looks at it oddly. Ready for it? "We don't accept these anymore." To that we said, "That's none of our concern. It's clearly noted on the card, "No exp." So then a manager is sent to our table. With NO pleasantries he barks, "When did you get this?!" We told him the event and the name of the charity and he said, "That was over two years ago!" We said, "No, actually a year and a half ago, and it's clearly marked, no expiration date." So he leaves in a gruff, huffing and puffing, while mumbling loud enough so we could hear how "unfair" it was and how he was going to "contact them and make them pay." (Contact the charity? That's really charitable of you, Mr. Manager!) It gets better. He comes back to the table with a receipt that he just printed saying, "This was only for $50." Oh wait a minute. We clearly ate more than $50 worth (not hard when Lamb Saag will put you back $25) knowing that we had $100 on the card. We started to argue and he literally pushed the receipt in our face. At this point he was getting really aggressive so I just gave him my credit card for the remaining $20. It doesn't stop there. Then he corners my husband after he's coming out of the bathrooms. (The bathrooms are really awkward by the way. The door to the bar faces the bathroom so while I washed my hands, bar patrons were watching. Creepy.) Anyway, he corners my husband (corners him!) and follows him back to our table and says, "This is from 2007." 2007? The event was in November 2010! In the end we said, "This is none of our concern. We won the certificate at an event. In the future, use expiration dates if you're not going to honor gifts you give to charities." He then stands over me after he handed me the credit card receipt to sign as if he wanted to see how much we'd tip them. (Right?) I look at him and say, "Excuse me, can you back off?" (I actually had to say that!) At this point, I was so tempted to do a runner and report them to the BBB. We did not leave a tip, which I have NEVER done in my life. If we get bad service I'll leave 15%, but my usual MINIMUM is 20%. I really was shocked at how this was handled. Bottom line: There is far better Indian in Philly for a fraction of the price. Don't assume that you're getting better service or a classier experience at this place for the prices. Go elsewhere. We will never go back. Notice how empty it is for dinner? There is a reason for that
label: NEG

It wasnt nearly as juicy as the competition, although it was slightly better seasoned. Chalk that up to the policy of cooking everything well-done. I respectfully disagree though, pointing to the reliance on multiple patties, melted cheese, and free toppings to create the illusion of moist, "juicy" texture. It probably doesnt matter to the masses though, as most people slather their burgers in ketchup, mayo, or whatever. However, the difference was obvious as daylight in this comparo, and should be noted. The american cheese used was plentiful and nicely melted, but lacked the exotic appeal of the vermont cheddar the competition featured. The grilled onions I had specified though were barely grilled at all, which seriously altered the flavor profile of this burger, not to mention added a crunch I didnt care for. Overall, the Five Guys burger was just OK by itself, but it was borderline disappointing when compared to the Elevation burger. After sampling both, I still wanted to go back and have another bite of that Elevation burger. In identical configurations, at identical prices, Five Guys didnt stack up to Elevation. However, while not offically considered in this comparison, Five Guys also allows a higher degree of customization with the availability of bacon and condiments like BBQ sauce - 2 things the competition lacks.

I enjoy my Herpes-free life. If that's your thing, though---as it seemed to be for a few older guys in Hawaiian shirts dancing as if trying to put out flames---then this might be your mecca. text: Lovely lunch today. I couldn't stop ordering. Got: 4 piece regular chicken meal (got 5 pieces, for whatever reason) order of livers 3 shrimp ($1 each) I was starving, not having eaten anything all day, and it was now nearly 2 p.m. Back at the office, ate the shrimp first with (as Steven has said) cocktail sauce in a squeeze package. The shrimp were good-sized, crunchy and crisp outside, tender and flavorful inside. Stayed crisp in transit, too. The cocktail sauce was I-don't-know-what! Next, the cole slaw, and (as Steven has said) it really does taste exactly like KFC. I love that! Rather small serving, so I gobbled that up. Next, a thigh of crispy-brown, juicy chicken (still warm) that was beautifully cooked (no red stuff near the bone, not overcooked dry) and tasted delicious. I "tasted" the mashed potatoes, which are clearly fake. I hate that, although I'm quite surprised they really didn't taste that bad, so maybe they're doctored in some way. Yellow gravy had an OK taste, albeit not a strong taste. The roll was a throw-away. The bread rack on wheels with all the plastic bags of rolls was sitting right out front, a clear indicator the rolls weren't home-made!! I tasted one liver, because I just couldn't resist, even though I was stuffed. It was divine. A little limp (from steaming in the box), but the breading flavor was good, and the liver wasn't over-cooked. There's a boat-load of chicken livers -- the 8x8x3-inch box was stuffed to the top! Considering the lunch damage, I've still got a massive bunch of livers, four pieces of chicken and a serving of mashed potatoes. How many meals is that? The whole shebang cost $14.07. Inside Porter's there's an ample ordering area. Eating space is four tables of four chairs, and four round elevated bar tables of two chairs. I don't think I'd consider eating in, but I'll surely get carryouts again! Thanks, Yelp! and Yelpers, for steering me to Porter's!! It's a find!

text: Very disappointed with Brazikat. Salad Bar - I've had better with more variety at most grocery stores! No hot food on the salad bar to be found at all. Every Brazilian Steakhouse I have ever been to has had a passable salad bar with at the least some Feijoada on it. Those crazy nasty little cheese biscuit things, what with that? Seriously!!! Stop serving these things now!! Either they were undercooked or they roll them in raw flour immediately after pulling them out of the oven. Beware of the bacon wrapped chicken!!!! I got two of them and they were both raw !! I brought this serious problem to the attention of the gaucho handing them out and with management and they both acted like it was no big whoop. The beef - Most of the beef was seasoned well and when it came out cooked properly it was tasty. Problem was that it was either Pittsburgh rare or the entire cut was over-cooked. Also be aware that they like making the rounds with the cheaper cuts of meat a whole lot more than the good stuff. Pro tip: Ask for a bowl of Chimichuri. The Caipirinha - They actually did know how to make them when I asked (Probably thanks to the previous yelper inquiring about them) but they are not making them correct. I could tell they had been watered down with a lemon lime soda when the only liquid that should be involved is the juice from the lime wedges and the Cachaça itself. I loves me some Caipririha when done correctly!! The service - The waiter was decent but one of the gauchos did a better job of taking care of us than he did. The one attentive gaucho was always asking how we liked the meal and if we needed anything. They also did not light the candle at our table nor did we ever see the mashed potatoes or baked bananas that some have mentioned. Word on the street is that another Churrascaria is opening in St. Charles. Hope they come into the area and do it right.
label: NEG

text: I've been looking forward to trying this place out for the last couple of weeks and the biggest draw was because it is family owned (I was told that by whoever runs their facebook page). First off it is really nice inside, very clean with a huge main dining area. When you first walk in there is a private dining area if you wanted to have a meeting or a party. Also their bar area (which is a decent size also) is in the back away from the main dining area with large screen TVs. They also have a nice outdoor dining area which overlooks the river. I liked how the tables had paper on them instead of table cloths (which I hope they recycle)....also crayons were provided to draw on the paper and the waitress wrote her name on it when we were seated so we would remember her name. I thought that was a good idea since I didn't see name tags. I ordered a couple appetizers; fried calamari (which was yummy, although I didn't really like either sauce that it came with it) and a salmon dish (which I didn't know was served cold - wish it would have stated that in the menu - it almost looked raw, even though I was assured it was cooked) but either way I didn't want it. I've never sent something back at a restaurant so I felt sort of bad but the staff said it was fine. As my entree, I ordered the fresh seared twin filets, topped with Maine lobster and asparagus in a lobster cream sauce with corn on the cob and veggies as my 2 sides. The steak was so good! Had a nice crisp outside and an almost melt in your mouth center. But I was not really impressed by the "sweet" corn, which really didn't taste like anything; I had 2 bites of and didn't finish the rest (brought it home for the groundhog in my backyard); it was almost like it wasn't cooked long enough. Also, the lobster cream sauce was just gross (I'm glad I asked for it on the side) I don't know if that's how it is supposed to taste because it was the first time I have ever had it. But the sauce took away the flavor of the lobster and I didn't even eat more than the first bite. Since it was my first time visiting the Big Fish Grill I was treated with a free dessert. I chose a piece of peanut butter pie. It was HUGE and really really good. It reminded me of those Asher's peanut butter eggs for Easter. If it wasn't for the atmosphere and how pleasant the staff were I would have probably given this place 1 star for the rating. The food fell flat (and the check was $80 for 2 people) and because of that I'm not sure if I will be returning.

text: I went to the newest location of Good Earth Cafe with my sister, Michelle, for lunch. She had told me only good things about this location and it was my first time trying a Good Earth Cafe so I thought why not? I expected it to be like most coffee shops: lots of varieties of coffee with limited food. I was hungry, so I figured I would be stuck having a muffin for lunch. However, I was so impressed the second I walked in. There was a huge variety of food items, that all sounded delicious! We ended up splitting their macaroni and cheese and a vegetarian breakfast panini. They both tasted awesome! The macaroni tasted like homemade macaroni and it was very tasty! The breakfast sandwich was interesting. It had a variety vegetables on it (what looked like eggplant and yellow peppers). I'm not such a fan of those types of vegetables so I just took them off. Still, there was a pesto sauce that made the sandwich so flavorful and scrumptious. The service was excellent! We weren't sure what type of drink to get. We just knew we wanted something slushy to enjoy in the sun. The girl behind the counter gave us a bunch of suggestions and we loved our drinks! I got the mocha frappe (yum!) and Michelle ordered the banana cafe frappe (double yum!). The drinks were frothy and not too sweet. The price was alright. It came to about $20 for two frappes, macaroni, and a breakfast panini. Walking into the restaurant, there was so much space! Lots of tables to sit at and huge counter space to look at the large variety of foods. The whole shop had a really nice, friendly atmosphere. Not like some coffee shops where everyone seems quite pretentious. We were hoping to enjoy some of the sun and were lucky enough to get a spot on their patio. With the sun shining and our delicious treats, it was a fabulous lunch experience! I already want to go back again and enjoy another meal on their patio. Just need a little more sunshine!! -Ashley Marie

text: I had never in my life thrown away a cupcake before I was done eating it until I tried one from Once Upon A Cupcake. I tried the Enchanted Cheesecake, which is a chocolate cake with a cheesecake filling and cream cheese icing. Sounds like my dream cupcake, right? Not so much. Maybe it was because I picked it up around 7 PM, but the cake was pretty dry. (Perhaps that's why most other cupcake shops around the city don't stay open so late?) The first bite was tasty and chocolate, but very dry. The other thing that hit me was the sugar overload. I like sweet things, but the sweetness of this cake was way too intense for my tastes. It took me a while to find the "cheesecake filling in the centre." When I found it, I was able to chow down on it in just one bite. I'm sure on its own, it would have been tasty, but it had so little sugar in it that it tasted almost bitter in comparison to the rest of the cake. If it was a bit sweeter, and the cake a little less so, they might have been a nice contrast to each other, but this was just gross. The cream cheese icing was good, but nothing worth writing home about. I finished the icing, but threw away the rest of the cake. At $4 a pop, this baby didn't come cheap, either. Bummer. A cute set-up (if a bit bland), cute cake names, and nice staff, but I say avoid!

text: Ladies. Wear white shirt and it most definitely will rain. Was in town for Mardi Gras. It was a buddy's bday weekend so an overall contingent of around 20 decided to meet in Nola for Mardi Gras, bday celebrations, general debauchery and well... Reverting back to 18 and acting like idiots. Maybe that was all redundant. I don't care. So it was Saturday morning. Mind you, I was in pain after Thurs night and all day drinkathon Friday. Not the arthritis in my right ankle from years of soccer pain. Nope, not that kind of pain. The ice pick in the temple, dehydration where you don't pee until 4pm kind of pain. Solution? Bloody Marys. So what do I do? I refuse to hit up Bourbon Street or Harrah's (eventhough I pummeled the Black Jack table into a bloody mess on Friday night). So I start walking from the Marriott. Aimlessly at first, but then down Royal. I have no idea where I'm going. John H don't care. John H just wants to eat shit and drink shit. John H is hurting and wants to curl up like the Honey Badger, but he still don't care. So I'm walking by this massive police station and reminded of times past in Nola and why I don't goto Bourbon Street even on Mardi Gras anymore. I keep walking. In the distance, I see the sign. It seems like the clouds parted and a ray of sunlight was shining on it. I figure either the Mardi Gras god's or the devil himself is pushing me towards this place. Maybe the Mardi Gras god's and Beezlebub are the same entity. Who cares. I walk in and I'm literally the only person in there. It is, afterall, like 10am Nola time. Shennanigans. I sit down and ask for my typical Ketel One and Bloody. They guy behind the bar quickly says, "sure you don't want to try it with the infused vodka"? He points towards the large jar full of all things peppery, garlic like, etc. I swear the damn thing had a light under it or maybe my vision was blurry due to lack of hydration. I say yes to this. Not knowing where this beginning of the day would take me. You see, I'm a gluton for punishment. I think my liver is just this awesome toy that kind of has a bypass around it. Put up yellow caution signs "road closed", alcohol please take the detour. NOPE. Just punish that sucker even more. Bloody Mary was the best one I've had in a while. So good I had two and one is usually all I need before moving on to different alcohol. Food was next on the list. Another bartender recommended their Chargrilled Oysters and Crab and Corn Bisque. "Ok, lady, don't give me any crap. Is it as good as Drago's or not". I didn't really say it like that because I think she would've three-finger pimped slapped me, but it was what I was thinking. She was awesome in her recommendations though. Ordered that very shit she recommended. First, the Crab and Corn Bisque. I want to free-base this stuff. Should've gotten the bowl. Just awesome. Then I moved onto Chargrilled Oysters. What happens when you combine large oysters, butter, spices, parmesan cheese and a grille? You come up with slap your mama good stuff. Not kidding, I would've slapped my mama if she tried to grab one off my plate. And yes, they were better than Drago's. As usual stupidity would allow, I decided to stay there another 3 hours while my friends trickled in. It was during this time that Mardi Gras monsoon 2012 decided to start. Have white shirt, will rain. Thank you to the group of 4 women who came in for lunch wearing white shirts after the deluge started. Your presence was noted and appreciated by all. Big eff you to the weather though. You rained out the Krewe of Tucks parade that we were all riding in. Good stuff. Try this place. Pretty damned cool and that upstairs balcony would be awesome during Friday happy hour or Saturday/Sunday afternoon.

I had seen a chiropractor a couple days before when we were in Portland, but I was still in pain and couldn't sleep at night. I was miserable, on the verge of tears! I found this place through Yelp and called as soon as I arrived in Boise. They were able to schedule an appointment for me within 15 minutes with Merlene. Merlene is someone who has met her calling and is the very best in her field as far as I'm concerned. She not only cured my ailments, she also helped me figure out what was causing my pain. She recommended pillow placements and some stretching that would help me sleep better. I haven't had any problems since! text: After checking in at the front desk, my friends (all guys) & I (a girl) went to the elevator and not two seconds later, a man resembling a bum said "hi how are you?" so we returned "good, how are you?" to which he replied "I am fairly intoxicated, and there's something I need to tell you." I was intrigued so I peaked out from behind my friends, the bum looks at me and says "cover your ears" and he continued "there is an excellent titty bar across from here". Good to know? Bf & I were in one room, our friends were in an adjacent, but not conjoined, room (11th floor, they "ran out of conjoined rooms" even though we requested it a month in advance). Crumbs and such on the carpet (bf said he could feel little objects under his feet since he was walking around in socks, instead of wearing flip flops like me). One of the lamps didn't have a light bulb in it, which was fine since there were 4 other lamps. Our room didn't have a "do not disturb" sign, so I called the front desk for one, the lady who answered said "uhhhhhh...okay....." and hung up (unprofessional), 10 mins later our sign arrived at our door (btw, the sign loves to fly off every time you open the door) The bed was large, big enough to fit 3 people comfortably, but it was stiff. Pillows were small but pretty fluffy. There were long dark hairs on one of the 4 pillows, I just pulled them off (at least they weren't pubic).There was a fold-out couch, old TV but at least it was a decent size and had enough channels to keep me entertained. Huge window, great view, had a set of sheer curtains and a set of thick curtains so not a single ray of sunlight came through in the morning. AC worked perfectly, there were like 3 settings so you could choose to have your room warm, a comfortable temperature, or completely freezing. The hallway leading to the room was always hot & humid so entering the room was a nice treat. The bathroom was decent. The shower curtain was definitely worn out (it's part plastic, part fabric, and the plastic part had so many rips). Water pressure was good, but the shower head made the water spray out in like 5 awkward streams, so I turned it to see what other options I had, but it was either that or 1 terribly hard stream in the center. The soap/lotion/shampoo smelled nice ("sugared citrus") but I preferred to use my own. So we went to our friends' room to hang out and the first thing I noticed was a dirty rolled-up sock on the ground by the bed, in plain sight. Disgusting. How did house keeping miss that? It didn't bother the guys, so oh well. Their room had two beds, I would say they could each fit 2 people comfortably. There was no couch. The toilet & sink were completely different than the ones in our room, which I thought was a little weird since hotel rooms are usually uniform. The walls are pretty thin, I could hear our friends in the next room, and the people on the other side of us. When our AC was off, it was like they were talking right next to me. No continental/complimentary breakfast, but it's not listed on their website so I didn't expect it anyway. There's a casino right across from the lobby. It's dinky. It smells of smoke but not as bad as Vegas. There's a 24 hr snack bar thing in the casino, though we didn't eat there. It's nice to know you have access to food all day, errrrryday. I liked seeing people walking around the hotel with their dogs. Made me miss my dog. According to other reviews, this hotel is pet-friendly. $55 per night for the room, plus state sales tax & local tax. State sales tax is 7.72% and local tax is 5.28% (doesn't have the percentages on the receipt so I calculated it for you guys). Overall, the bad outweighs the good: poor customer service, dirty rooms, the entire hotel needs an update (not just the rooms), blah blah blah. I stayed here because an event I attended was being held here, but I would definitely not stay here again.

text: My wife and I went on a tapa style restaurant crawl over the weekend starting at Barbuzzo (which was as delicious as ever). Towards the end of our meal we asked our bartender about any good restaurant recs in the area, and he mentioned that The Oyster House on Sansom had just undergone some sort of renovation/change in ownership and it was GOOD. (Not sure how long ago this happened, but I vaguely remember reading a review in the Inquirer a while back). Anyway, being a beautiful June evening we wandered the few blocks down Sansom, and walked into the Oyster House. The place was hopping, and just before we sat down I noticed the specials board stated that they were running $1 Happy Hour oysters from 9-11 pm on Saturday. It was Saturday, and about 7:30pm, so being the cheap bastard that I am, we left and carried on down the street to Tinto (review soon to come), and The Dandelion Pub (battle rap style review soon to come). Upon our return, the place was jammed. Not a seat was to be had at the enormous bar that snakes it's way through the whole restaurant. The place was crowded with a mix of couples out on the town (like us), tables of friends, and a smattering of hipsters. Nobody was overly dressed, and very few people looked like they had just rolled out of bed. The two lovely hostesses promptly took my name, told us to grab a drink if we wanted, and that they would find us as soon as two seats opened up. Once at the bar, I had to inquire about the champagne special. Apparently, it comes in a can. I declined, and ordered a $3 Preininger, I mean Kenzinger, and my wife had a glass of house white. Both of us approved of our drinks. I had never had Kenzinger before, and found it a crisp refreshing pilsner perfectly suited for the weather, and some oysters. Speaking of oysters, the bartender told us that the $1 Happy Hour special only refers to the oyster of the day, which was a Delaware Bay oyster, not a choice of any of the 6 other oysters they offer. Being unsure of whether I have ever tried a Delaware Bay oyster, I was almost as apprehensive about the prospect of eating something out of the scummy Delaware Bay as I was about the champagne in a can. After quickly being seated at the bar, my wife and I both agreed that we'd be brave, and order just 6 of them in case they were repulsive. Thankfully, they were not, and we quickly ordered six more. The oysters were medium in size, had very low salinity, and were extremely creamy in the mouth. I liked them. Can't believe I just wrote the line, creamy in the mouth, but dammit they were. My only gripe was that the oysters were not fully shucked, and were still attached to the shell. Also, there was absolutely no oyster liquor in the shell. Not sure if it that is due to the kind of oyster, but I like the juice. Being the last stop on the tapa crawl, we decided to call it a night, but vowed we'd return for more. Apparently, they offer something called "Tuesday Night Dump Dinner". As unappetizing as it sounds, it looks like a Pile O' Seafood. I am good with that. And for 19 bucks, I am good with that, too. I definitely, enjoyed our brief snack, and was impressed with the fantastic service from both hostesses, and bartenders. The bartenders were swamped, but they handled it with ease, and personable service. Also, loved the seafood house decor with a myriad of oyster plates decorating the walls. We are both excited to return, and will hopefully make it back for Dump Night.
label: POS

text: Dear people of Chinatown (and those who venture into it), Mandarin and Szechuan does not mean Taiwanese. I'm not even sure if the staff here is Taiwanese. I had asked them if they had "Dan Bing" and they looked at me like I wanted an enchilada. Back me up here, my fellow Taiwanese! But, they do have some dishes from Taiwan on the menu. With that settled, let's get to the good (and bad) stuff. Definitely Order: + Peking Noodle (Ja Jiang Mien) - This is the reason I love coming here. This is the Chinese version of Spaghetti alla Bolognese. Salty, sweet, spicy, crunchy bean sauce over thick Chinese noodles. The noodles are on the softer side (old school Asians don't believe in al dente) and mix very well with the sauce. + Scallion Pancake - The best scallion pancake in the city. It's not thick like other places, and it's thin enough where it's not a cracker, either. The best part is the dipping sauce. Instead of the standard black vinegar mixture, the sauce is clear! I think it tastes better than its dark counterpart. + Ma Po Tofu - I love ma po tofu. When I can't have my mom's, I come here for it. Maybe Order: + Taiwan Beef Noodle Soup - The noodle soup tastes pretty authentic, although it is on the blander side. + Pai Goo Fan - Fried pork chops w/ pickled veggies over rice. I like this one, but the pork chops need to be crispier. Don't Order: + Soup Dumplings - Tastes like the frozen kind. There are other spots in town if you're craving these little exploding dumpling balls. + Chinese-American Dishes - General Tso's chicken, beef and broccoli, orange chicken, and shrimp in lobster sauce? Umm... no. I just noticed that all of the dishes listed under "Maybe" are the Taiwanese dishes, weird. The service, food, and prices at Empress Garden are great. Now if I can only find a place that makes Dan Bing....

text: I have a long review written but here is the short version: Food: 2 out of 5 stars- well conceived but poorly executed dishes. HUGE portions, which in my opinion is a sign of subpar food. Thus started and evening of sincere disappointment. The tables meant for 2 are completely too small- after our drinks, chips and salsa, and appetizer were all on the table- there was literally no room. So much so, our server stacked our chip bowl between the two salsa bowls. Every maneuver had to be carefully thought out as not to spill something. I'm not sure if we caught the kitchen on an off day or perhaps an off hour. We started with the Costillitas for an appetizer. The ribs were old and dried out. I suspected that had been cooked previously in the day if not on an earlier day and been reheated. The sauce was very very thickened and dried to the plate (as if sat under a heat lamp or nuked in the microwave). Even the salsa had evidence of sitting out to dry. Then entrees- I ordered the Tinga Poblana de Cerdo, which is essentially a pork shoulder, chorizo, and potato stew. Again it definitely was evident that the order had been microwaved (Plate was too hot to touch, stew was MOLTEN hot and a slight crust had formed around the top rim). I can expect, even hope, a stew to be prepared in advance and left cooking all day (mmmm ) but it was my suspicion it had been prepared another day, refrigerated, then reheated for me. My girlfriend ordered the Mahi Mahi. It was quite fishy and probably one of the driest pieces of fish i've ever eaten. Both entrees also came with a massive amount of throw-away sides like reheated rice and veggies. In my mind- it seemed like we came at an off hour. I am going to give them the benefit of the doubt and say MAYBE they cook to order during normal dinner hours and perhaps we came too early that we caught them at a bad time. One thing is for sure. I know when my order is made-to-order and when it has been reheated. i can say for 90% certainty that every single thing i consumed that day had been cooked on a previous date and my chef for the day was a commercial microwave. I would consider giving them another chance to taste some of these dishes when they are fresh, but unfortunately, with so many great choices in philly for good food, i can say I wont be back by my own choosing.

text: I was so excited to have a lunch date yesterday with one of my Yelp friends, Ms. Tracey W. When Yelpers get together, it is always so hard to pick a place to go. Being a gentleman, I told Tracey she could pick. She thought we should go some place new for both of us and doing that with two active Yelpers can be a challenge. After extensive debating, we selected The Fountain on Locust. I had been there once before, but was waiting for a second visit before reviewing and Tracey W. had it on her bucket list. TFL is a ice cream shop for adults. The menu of Martinis make me droll, I wanted a Dreamciscle Martini so bad, it just sounds luscious. Tracey W and I did have several good giggles. Starting off with our waiter having to come to our table multiple times just to get our order. Then posing our malt, shake and sandwiches for their closeups. I told Tracey on my first visit I had alcohol, but this time I wanted to experience a shake/malt. When you're at a soda fountain, you've got to experience a hand made shake and TFL does it oh so right. Every since I was a wee lad I have loved malt flavoring and the best malts are chocolate. Tracey went with a shake and choose chocolate too. I like the touch of bringing you the extra pour in the stainless mixing glass. Both of our drinks made that funny noise, when your straw has nothing else to pull up. That is a sign of a good drink, not bad manners. For lunch I had the Hot Roast Beef Melt and it was near orgasmic. I am a big beef eater and am partial to Angus Beef, which this is made from. Those big black cows, paid for my college education. This sandwich is savory Angus beef with white cheddar and grilled onion. It is served on a fresh baked baguette, that has Subway uttering, "how do they do that". It is also served with a house made horseradish sauce. I use to not be a fan of horseradish, but theirs has changed my mind and I'd buy in a jar if were available. (hint-hint) As a side I choose the Orange Onion Salad with Poppyseed Dressing. It is what the name says, oranges and red onion and nothing else. There is no lettuce in this salad. Once again, TFL impressed me with their house made dressing. It totally blew me away & I have family in the salad dressing business. Tracey's sandwich looked equally impressive. She was the perfect "girl" date ordering a Mixed Salad Sandwich. She was right in her review, saying the shake really didn't go with the food. However, we drank & ate what we wanted. Visualize a fresh baguette with melted Parmesan and Mozzarella Cheeses then stuffed with mixed lettuces, roasted red pepper, tomato, artichoke and a smear of house made pesto. You can make it St. Louis Style by adding meat (chicken), which Tracey did. I will order that sandwich on my next visit. I was tempted by her side salad which was the Stutz Salad, but I would have had to have them hold the walnuts. Not nuts about that nut. Otherwise, baby spinach, plump Mandarin oranges, goat cheese and a creamy marmalade dressing would be a perfect summer salad. Tracey W. mentioned our next outing we would drink and I must say that is great, but it also scares me. Without booze, we still managed to share family/life secrets. I'd be scared to see what we'd share if we had Vodka & beer in us. In closing if Tracey would have suggested ice cream for lunch, I would have called dibs on the Banana Split.

With some spicy barbecue sauce on it, it was better. The chicken was pretty good -- rubbed with spices and cooked to a nice finish. The potato salad consisted of slightly undercooked potatoes and mayonnaise: after a bite, I abandoned it. The broccoli was plain, but properly cooked (neither under nor overcooked) and tasty. The corn muffin was the best part of the meal: moist, slightly sticky, sweet and tasty. My husband reported that the pork ribs were decent, but nothing special. He was underwhelmed by the brisket as well. His beans tasted good (I tried them). The coleslaw was okay, fresh but not imaginative or interesting. His verdict: the ice cream sundae was the best part of the meal. The service was quite decent -- casual, friendly, and exactly as I'd expect of a barbecue place. The decor was overdone pseudo-Texas, again exactly as I'd expect of a barbecue place. :-) I suspect that this place would go over well for a crowd of non-foodie, non-barbecue lovers who didn't grow up in Texas, but I'm a hard sell with barbecue. text: i was finally able to check this place out. yay for new orleans' first ethiopian restaurant! it's a quaint little establishment on magazine near louisiana, and you'd miss it if you weren't looking for it (or had a rad gps like i do!) it appears it is in an old converted house and feels a lot like the common room of one of those crazy zealot churches (where's my kool aid?) or a less cozy and warm country grandma's digs (due to the fluorescent lights - which i *hate* - and large screen tv.) so, the four stars is solely for the dining atmosphere and not the food. and the food - it was terrific! if you've read any of my yelp reviews, i'm the resident gluten-intolerant reviewer and have had varying experiences while dining out. i told the (overworked but uber sweet) waitress that i was gluten-free, and she recommended dishes and was SUPER accommodating. text: As far as Chinese food goes near UPenn, this place is probably as good as it gets for reasonable prices. The service is quick and dry, you can go in solo without looking too pathetic, and the complimentary tea (I'm assuming it's some variety of oolong) is usually hot (and not lukewarm), which is admittedly a plus. I've ordered both take-out and eat-in. I've often gotten the lunch special which goes for $6.95 dine-in and $5.95 take-out. The fried rice is dry and veggie-only for the lunch special, but if you order it a la carte it looks tastier (the rice looks less parched and more freshly prepared rather than desiccated from sitting out too long in a giant stainless steel tub). I haven't ordered the fried rice a la carte, though, so you should probably share an order with a friend for dinner. The lunch special can also come with brown rice which I haven't tried yet. I recommend the following dishes: 1) Eggplant in garlic sauce with chicken 2) Shrimp egg foo-young 3) Pan-fried noodles (veggie or chicken - the beef brisket has a strange after-taste and can get stuck in your teeth). Do not get the sesame chicken - it looks artificially orange (and not the burnt orange color one would normally associate with the dish). It is also too sweet for my tastes. The duck noodle soup is decent, but nothing special, and something I'd probably get if the season were winter. I will give two grades (one for service, one for taste): Service: B Taste: B- This was my first review, so please let me know if any additional information is needed.

text: I will start this review by saying that the only reason this is even a two star is because of one of their employees, Anjay. I booked this hotel on priceline for a one night stay. I was taking my brother up for a really short visit to see my alma mater, the University of South Florida. This hotel is about 5 minutes from the campus and conveniently located near I-75, and it's in a nice area of Temple Terrace. I got a great deal on priceline. It was about half off what the other sites had, and more like 60% off the rate to book directly with Hilton. I expected much more from the Hilton brand. We called on our way to Tampa to see what rooms they had available, and to see if we could snag a double. As someone who has worked in the travel industry, I knew that we may have had to make some sacrifices on our room, but it can't hurt to ask and call ahead. The first two employees I encountered seemed to have the attitude of "you get what you pay for", rather than giving good customer service. One of the women was either a supervisor or seemed more experienced than the other, and this created some chaos when we checked in. The first employee was going to upgrade us and the other stopped her because we booked third party, so we "get what they have left"...This meant we got a king sized bed rather than two doubles and a smoking room for two non smokers that have pretty bad reactions to cigarette smoke. Fantastic. We figured we would see how things went before making a big deal about anything. They sent us up to a room on the 6th floor, the smoking floor. As soon as we got out of the elevator, we were hit with a strong stench of cigarettes. My eyes were immediately irritated and my throat started to close up. When I opened the door to our room, the bed was unmade, and there were clothes and a laptop on it. I quickly closed the door, and headed downstairs. The women at the desk seemed confused and then realized they had put someone in that room and then changed their room, but the person hadn't taken all of their stuff yet. The ruder employee of the two told me to just go back up to the room, and I told her again that the bed was unmade and asked if someone could come clean the room. She looked at me like I had just made the most ridiculous request, and then gave us a key to the room across the hall. Our second room still had the king bed and cigarette issue, but at least it was vacant. We opened a window and left for a few hours to see if that would help the smoke situation. When we came back, it was still unbearable. I went downstairs and asked the employee that just came on for the next shift, Anjay, if he could help us in any way. He said that they were oversold, and he didn't have any rooms to move us to, so he had someone send up their "ozone" machine that is supposed to eliminate the smoke smell. They do this on cruise ships, and I know it usually works, so we waited in the lobby while they worked on our room. The hotel does have free wifi, so we were able to lounge for a bit, and I used that time to look up hotels in the area. I knew that it was better to pay $100 for a new hotel than to come back to Miami feeling sick and missing work or going to the doctor. I was already starting to feel ill from the short time that we were in the room, so I knew that sleeping there was not an option. While we were waiting in the lobby, I heard Anjay telling people they were oversold and helping people that booked direct find a room at local Hilton chains. After about an hour, we went back to our room and although it smelled better, that smoke was still there. I called Anjay and asked if he could do anything and that I was willing to pay for an upgrade. He knew of a family that wanted a smoking room, but with double beds. He called them anyways to see if they wanted to switch and just get a roll-away bed for their son. At first they declined, but 5 minutes later, Anjay called back and said they wanted to switch. Thank goodness! We swapped keys, and I went up to our new room. Smoke free! Was it problem free? Nope. The thermostat was broken so we had limited options with the A/C unit, one of the lamps wouldn't stay on so we just kept it off, and the TV was fuzzy and had lines through it. Other than that, everything was fine so I wasn't going to complain about the little things. We were comfortable and able to breathe, and I was satisfied with our room. For the rest of our stay, everything was fine, but that mess in the beginning set a really negative tone for the trip. I'm so thankful that Anjay was so hard working and actually made the effort to get us into a non smoking room. It saved us a headache and money because we were so close to just heading to another hotel in the area. After the trip, Hilton sent me an email saying they have a "Best Price Guaranteed" program where they will match prices from travel sites. It may be worth looking at because this hotel seemed to favor direct guests.

text: Not at all what we Expected -- Definately NOT Spanish! Came here with high expectations for our 22nd Anniversary. Expecting a Spanish style Tapas restaurant -- one of our favorite cuisines -- but that's not what we got. Being from Chicago originally, where there are some excellent authentic Spanish-style Tapas Restaurants -- and, also have visited and lived in Spain, we know what we're talking about. To start with, the decor is all over the place, with the only thing reminiscent of Spain being a some framed photos on the wall. Even the much-too-loud music playing, was not spanish or mexican or anything close. (Rosas next door, looked and sounded more Spanish than this -- and, which we first mistakenly walked into, thinking it was Alcazar). We wanted to start with -- as we traditionally do -- a nice glass of our favorite Fino Sherry from Tio Pepe. The Waitress didn't even know what we were talking about. 'Fortunately' my wife spotted the bottle on the bar shelf alongside the whiskeys and vodkas. (Even more amazingly, it was apparently the only Sherry they had). However, not only was it not chilled, it had been already been opened (about a glass missing). And, based on the waitress telling us she 'never knew they had it' ... it might have been sitting there opened for months. We had her chill a glass for us anyway to try it ... yuck. Spoiled as expected. Tried to explain to her it was essentially a wine, that once opened must be consumed within a couple of days (unless you have a preserving system). I think my advice 'flew over her head', because she just put the bottle back on the shelf (instead of disposing of it). (Oh, and she served it in a mini-Champagne glass ???). Next, we reviewed the wine list for something else -- lo and behold -- not a single Spanish Wine on the menu ('closest' they had was one Argentine wine from Mendoza, but of course that wasn't chilled either, so she offered us an SB haut that was ok ,albeit pricey at $9/glass). As for the menu and purported 'Tapas', well we couldn't find anything I would consider Spanish. More Italian and French style than anything, with a majority being cheese-centered (which is ok, as long as you like and can eat cheese), and lots of pizza/flat-bread appetizers. We did try the baked goat-cheese 'tapa' which was alright, and the Mushrooms in sherry sauce. The only problem with the Mushroom dish (which I also thought was fairly good), was they didn't bother to offer any sliced bread to eat it with and soak up the sauce (as is expected in any traditional Spanish Tapas restaurant) ... and, we had to ask twice to get some. We were so dissappointed that we left after that, not even having a complete meal. Good news is, our Anniversary dinner was not spoiled, because we walked across the street to the Thai Restaurant which was fabulous (see our next review). Bottom Line: This is NOT a Spanish Tapas Restaurant as one would assume; the servers and bartender are friendly but clueless; the decor and menu have no consistent theme; ... But, if you are looking for a basic California-style Bar and restaurant then its okay/average albeit pricey in our opinion.

text: Possibly my first 5 star review. Actually 4.75 stars, but I'll round up In a nutshell - near perfect familiar food; excellent, although not real friendly service, and reasonable prices. I was very hungry coming in to this restaurant, so I may have been biased by my appetite, but the food was great. - One would never know there was a great restaurant inside based on the non-nondescript exterior of Bern's in Hyde Park neighborhood of Tamps. Inside, the decor is old-school steakhouse with dark ambiance, several small dining rooms, decorated with spanish renaissance and 17th century art in ornate gold frames. Very comfy and warm. - The cocktails at the bar were good. Lovely, cozy bar. It was populated mostly with business people (I actulally ran into a colleague from years ago) and an older clientele (it is Florida). - Given the entrees come with many sides already, I insisted we try an appetizer. The duck confit with pomegranate reduction and arugula was awesome. I don't usually like the sweetness and richness of most duck dishes, but this appetizer - a leg/thigh on bone was perfectly balanced. and the pomegranate wasn't there just to be trendy - it really worked with the duck. - The best French onion soup I ever had. Not too cheesy not too salty - just right. It was a nice inclusion to the entree (not a la carte), and the serving size wasn't so big it filled me up before the meal. - The entree ALSO came with a perfect organic side salad. I chose a white balsamic vinaigrette that was obviously made with top notch oil and vinegar. The organic, farm fresh veggies were obviously better than anything one can get at publix. - I was finally getting full when the entrees came. I ordered red snapper on a bed of arugula and mashed potatoes. Very good, on par with most fish dishes I've had at better restaurants. - The entrees also came with a side of perfectly cooked onion rings and a nice bright veggie side which tonight was carrots and cucumbers (or was it zucchini?) Not sure, but it was good.. - Mom got shrimp scampi. It was phenomenal. It was a traditional jumbo shrimp scampi, with a florida/caribbean twist. It reminded me of Belize with the hint of mango and coconut. The best entree of the three. -Dad got Chateau Briand. It was good, and apparently a Bern's favorite. . I'm not crazy about steak but for steak it was perfectly done. Mom and dad both had a baked potato side. - I had Jordan and Cakebread Chardonnays with my meal. They were reasonably priced at under $15 a glass. Total bill for the 3 of us with drinks came to a very reasonable $220, 12% gratuity included. (Typically I would never order an app and 3 sides with my entree. At Mortons, that would be much higher!) We then took the kitchen/wine cellar tour which was a good break before dessert. The tour only took a few minutes,so if you're wondering whether to do it, just do it. Its a nice break between dinner and dessert upstairs. The dessert floor had cozy individual table areas where dessert is ordered a la carte and offered a new experience for the evening. It also had this cute little jukebox like thing where you could ask for service, or select from one of 5 music selections. We splurged on dessert. Although we could have easily split one or two generously sized desserts, we each ordered something. I got " figs and cheese" which was a trio - fig compote on sweet lady fingers, cut fig on blue cheese cheesecake, and my favorite, another fig compote on a small crispy/soft sweet warm biscuit that was a little piece of heaven. I paired my dessert with a 30 year tawny port. Just as the server described, it was a nice middle ground between a sweet dessert and a cheese option. The menu had a long list of cheeses - to go with the selection of many thousands? of wines on the list. Dad got "Chocolate Lush". Apparently it was so good he didn't share. A rich chocolate tort served with ice cream & warm chocolate sauce Mom, once again placing the winning order, got macadamia ice cream in waffle cone. It was the servers recommendation, and the best of the three desserts we ordered. Delicious chocolate-based ice cream with crisp macadamias and the best waffle cone I ever had, obviously made in the kitchen. For someone who isn't really big on steakhouses, I loved Bern's. It was a wonderful surprise. They obviously has the food dialed in. They set pretense and experimentation aside for solid dishes that taste good. Regarding service, the servers did everything right, Timing was perfect, and the main server was always there for us, not leaving the busboys to ask us for water or drinks. However - they weren't super warm and friendly. I guess part of that is east coast persona, and working in the same restaurant for years will do that . Bonus points to our dessert server who personally ran down my leftover blue cheese cheesecake to the valet since I left it on the table. Yummy!

I have been here with a large party for my Birthday and the server was nice but inept, another time our entree came out the same time as our appetizer, but this time the server was downright rude, I don't think she wanted to be there. She barely greeted us and rattled off the specials so fast that I don't even know what they were except that there was "duck prosciutto" when I said questioningly "duck prosciutto?" she just kept going. As far as I know prosciutto means Italian ham so I was intrigued and may have ordered it if she would have elaborated. So we ordered our appetizers and everything came out quickly and the guy who delivered it was very nice. We had the meatballs and the crisp potatoes. The meatballs were burnt on the outside and the potatoes were nothing special but the sauces on both were delicious and the foccacia was yummy too! Our server came back to take our entree order and again she acted like she couldn't wait to get away! Now, I am not rich, so Campo is mostly a special occasion restaurant for me. However... I was a professional cook for 25 years and so I like to go where the quality of food and service is great and I tip 20 to 25% when I am happy. I started out bussing tables at 15 and worked my way back to the kitchen doing every job in between so I know how hard this business is! We ordered the kale salad, Margherita pizza and the gnocchi with winter squash, again everything was delivered promptly by very polite servers. The kale salad was absolutely delicious. The sauce on the gnocchi was sublime, but the gnocchi was a little dense,but I am kind of a snob when it comes to Italian food, growing up in an Italian family, but really most people wouldn't even notice. The Margherita was exactly as it should be; thin crust, tomato, basil and mozzarella although there could have been a little more cheese. Pizza shouldn't be drowned in cheese but some of the pieces on this pizza didn't have any at all! Next we requested the dessert menu and again this server acted like she did not want to be there. She threw one menu on the table and didn't explain what flavors of ice cream and sorbet there was or what the chef's trio was. We waited about 10 minutes and she never came back so I grabbed one of the employees who had asked us if everything was alright previously. He seemed to be very busy helping to bus and clean tables, but was kind enough to explain the menu and help us decide what we wanted. We got a trio of sorbet's, I always love there blood orange, but the cherry had this great intense flavor and my niece loved the passion fruit. The server who helped us with dessert happened to be the Owner Mark, had he not intervened our experience would have been really bad and I might not have come back. I admire an owner who pitches in and maybe they have been short handed when I have been there, but I hope he figures out what is going on because I really want to love this place! Reno doesn't have that many great restaurants and I want this one to succeed!

text: I have been going to this restaurant since it opened. The food is spectacular; some of the best and most authentic Japanese food I have ever had outside of Japan. And until last night, the service has always been good. Unfortunately, Yoshimatsu now has a manager working for them who is under the impression that his job is to disrespect and belittle his customers. Last night two friends and I went to dinner at around 6:30. The restaurant was perhaps half full. We ordered, and waited. And waited. After 20 - 30 minutes, I asked our very nice waitress how much longer we would be waiting for our food. She walked to the counter and spoke to a man who had just been standing there the whole time, not helping her, and not helping the cashier. Our waitress came back and informed us that it would be at least ten more minutes. The man at the counter - whom I am assuming was the manager - mumbled to her that it could actually be closer to 20 more minutes. I approached him, and asked for a refund, since we were hungry, and did not want to wait 40 - 50 minutes for our food. This man immediately became loud and abusive. He told me that good, "handmade food" always takes at least 20 minutes, and what did I expect? I informed him that I had been coming to this restaurant since it opened, and I never had to wait this long. He ignored me, offered no apology or excuse, and said that their kitchen always takes this long. He was intent on doing nothing but arguing with me, and loudly proclaiming to all within earshot how I was being unreasonable. I asked him if he was or was not going to give me a refund. He shrugged again, said "well you can ask the cashier," then turned his back to me, and loudly told the kitchen "these people want a refund because they don't want to wait for good food." I do not think it is too much to expect to be served within 20 minutes at a half-full, casual-service restaurant. And even if one assumes for a moment that my expectations were too high, what business vocally belittles and abuses its customers? I work very hard for my money, and I do my best to patronize local businesses. Experiences like this make me question why on earth a business wants to stay open in the first place. If you have such disrespect for the people whose money keeps you open, if you are so quick to display such public disdain for your customers, why not just close up shop? It is not my privilege to eat at your restaurant. You are doing me no favors by allowing me to walk through your doors. I used to love this restaurant, and bring many friends here. It will be very hard for me to go back. Call me crazy, but being belittled and openly mocked by restaurant staff leaves a bitter taste in my mouth, that makes me very hesitant to return.

text: Perfection. I came to Bourbon House for a wedding rehearsal dinner and couldn't help but think the space was absolutely wonderful. I told the bartender to just make me something really strong and really delicious with vodka, which proceeded to be a rum punch with vodka instead of rum and it was fan-freaking-tastic. Just what the doctor ordered. Dinner was flawless, too. Appetizers of fried eggplant and zucchini were fairly standard, however, the gumbo was to die for as was the BBQ shrimp served with seasonal veggies and mashed potatoes. Very rich, excellent sauces and exceptionally delicious seafood. Service was amazing, too, as I've come to expect from New Orleans. It's such a tourist town with a surprisingly small actual population, so I get the feeling that every restaurant in town knows that they're dealing with guests of the city for the most part and wants visitors to really enjoy their New Orleans experience. I dig that. Lastly, Bourbon House is obviously in a great spot for barhopping after dinner.

A good thing to know, if someone in your group doesn't like seafood, their cheeseburger might be the best in town. Very good. You can check out their menu on line. Dinners are $20+ but well worth it. They don't skimp on the quality or quantity plus the servers and bussers don't give you a chance to run out of drinks, coffee, bread or anything. They're right on top of things. Enjoy

text: Awesome Awesome Awesome. Just as good as I remembered it from restaurant week in January! Went in on a Saturday night, incredibly crowded, but to our luck, four spots opened up right on the corner of the bar which was perfect! The meal? Absolutely amazing! Want to hear our dishes? I thought you'd never ask... Korean BBQ Beef Satay - yum yum, bbq beef, tasty Edamame Dumplings - soft and not too chewy, in the sake broth Crispy Brussel Sprouts - the fish sauce totally made this dish, amazing to go with the bitterness of the brussel sprouts "Philly Cheese Steak" - Spicy and tasty and salty and cheesy all at once! Calamari Salad - Fresh greens, tangy sweet sauce, and light and airy fried calamari, so good Seared Tuna - Peppery outside, sushi grade inside, on a plate with a sweeping brush of soy sauce Charred Thai Chicken - Some tasty spicy chicken, some daikon, and some crisp watercress Shrimp Pad Thai - quite possibly my favorite dish in all of Philadelphia! Massive shrimp, lots of peanuts, and just all around amazingness! Homemade soft-serve ice cream? Sure, the perfect way to finish off a meal! Can't wait to go back again for the shrimp pad thai ASAP! Service was pretty good for being at the bar after we ordered, but took a few minutes to get our food and drink orders. Definitely need to get back here again within the next few weeks!

text: I used to love this place- in the neighborhood, great service ( Adrian was the very best server!), and good food at a fair price. Now, the place is still in my neighborhood, and Adrian still works there, but that is all that this restaurant has in common with the place it used to be. Gone are the inviting and oh-so-cozy booths in the dining area. These nests of closeness have been moved to the bar to face the TV ( how thrilling). The diners are left with small tables that have red lamps on them. And the lamp cords run right across the table. Granted, the cords are taped down, but still, who wants a brown snake of electric wire sneaking across the dinner table? Not me. The whole vibe is a bit too bordello for my liking. Which brings me to the the largest problem. Wantanabe has gone from fun family hang-out spot to pretentious dining establishment. Granted, John, our waiter did the best he could with what he had to work with, but still. He remembered me and my child from prior visits to the old Wantanbe and at Batter'd and Fried. But is all this frou-frou really necessary? And after eating lack luster sushi, I brought my concerns about the atmosphere and lack of family dining options to the manager. It would not have been possible for the manager to care any less about my feedback. Really. He looked me right in the eye as if I were speaking another language, and dismissed me with his ennui. The manager did not engage me with questions, ask my opinions, or make even the slightest attempt to respond to my oberservations. It is a pity that the feed back of diners matter so little to the people that run Wanatabe. I asked the hostess what happened to the kid menu, and she said, "well, there is a little one." Little indeed. So little that it was not offered to me when I sat down. With my kid. And we were the only people eating in the dining area. No other customers came in to sit down and eat the whole time I was there. You'd figure they'd be happy to have us. So, unfortunately, I cannot and do not recommend this place. With or without a child. You'd be better off going to the amazing Mitchell's Deli for dinner, where they remember you, care about you and value your business, or perhaps visiting the new Riverside Pharmacy for a snack. Perhaps a breath mint to get the taste of dyspepsia out of your mouth after eating at Wantanabe.

She was willing to take my feedback and make adjustments, but even then the job wasn't complete. She didn't do a thorough job and didn't have a very refined technique, which results in a lot of stopping/starting. The reason they are able to charge this much is because there is no competition for this service in Philadelphia. If this place was in NYC (where I used to live until a few weeks ago) they wouldn't really survive because there are a lot of places who provide more skilled technicians for a lot less. I'm okay with paying for anything, as long as I believe the service is of the highest quality. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case here. I will say that the preparation of the food does take a little bit of time. I've had to wait in line for 10-15 minutes before I get up to order (depending on how busy it is) but the employees are friendly and conversational, so it doesn't feel like they want you to get in, order, and get out like SOME places... Did you catch that I was referencing Subway, Quizno's, and/or Port of Subs? I was. I love that the guys at Togo's will talk to you and know the importance of having a good time while being great at their job. However, a subsequent epidural injection provided only about five days of pain relief, so the expensive procedure was largely in vain. text: If you're looking for good, authentic, and affordable North Indian food, look no further. I'm Indian and, naturally, quite picky about Indian restaurants. My friend and I stumbled upon this place and decided to give it a shot. And I am so glad that we did. Korma in most Indian restaurants in the US caters to the tastes of Americans who can't handle spice. Not so here. It's not too spicy--Korma isn't quite meant to be--but it's not the bland, sweetish, creamy dish one finds at all to many Indian restaurants. The spices are nicely balanced and it's creamy and mild in just the right proportions. The Saag Paneer, again, was really great. I didn't have to dig for bits of paneer as I often have to at buffets! The vegetable dishes were also great. My friend was blown away by the Goat curry. I was also delighted to find Limca and Thums Up here--anyone who's grown up in India will know why! We also got nice fresh naan at our table and our waiter gladly got us more and insisted that we eat the hot, fresh naan instead of finishing the basket of cold naan. He was very friendly and attentive. I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could because I was completely unimpressed by the buffet desserts. Maybe the a la carte desserts are better, though. Anyhow, next time I'm craving real Indian food and I'm too lazy to cook it myself, I'm headed here.

The second member of our party tried the General Tso's Chicken with white rice and Wonton soup, found the taste to be very mediocre and a bit dry as well. The third member of our part had the Thai Red Curry with Chicken (and Wonton soup). He too thought it was very bland and mediocre. He described it as if they slapped together some vegetables and chicken and just added curry sauce to it. They said their Wonton soup to be good, but then again, how can you possibly mess up Wonton soup? The final member of our party had some sushi. He has the some Spicy Tuna rolls (he said this was pretty good), and some Tuna and Salmon Nigiri (not the freshest, just mediocre). The overall presentation of the sushi was pretty bad (the large plate was too big for the amount of sushi he got). He felt that the rice was a bit dry and had been sitting for a while. The miso soup he got with his sushi was okay, but the side salad the actually good. Overall, it seems that this place tries is trying to cater to too many tastes (large menu, varied tastes) at the same time, but they stretch themselves too thin and fail at all of them (this have all the typical dishes of a Chinese restaurant, but not even the most basic a dishes are any good). The owners should put more work on improving the quality of their dishes than the quantity of their selection. Some of the dishes could have have been a bit cheaper ($2-3) of match their overall quality. If you're a good Chinese or Japanese place, look somewhere else. I personally left the place very disappointed. As a side note, parking in the small shopping center where the restaurant is located is very tight (especially around noon or in the evening). text: Ok...so I live in the neighborhood, and have friends who absolutely LOVE this place. I'm rarely in the mood for music so loud I can't hear the person next to me, but I've been a few times, because I enjoy the outdoor seating and the opportunity to people watch. The food is average, the service is pretty sub-par (whoever said it seems like the entire staff is nursing a collective PBR-induced hangover hit the nail on the head). But the bar at PYT can be a fun spot, if you happen to walk in on a day when it's not overflowing with hipster wannabes who have taken the day off from Sea Isle to guzzle beer and fist pump in their neon sunglasses (circa 1987). I've actually had some borderline nice experiences at the bar at PYT. The DJs they have are actually very talented, and I love the eclectic mix of 80s music, old school hip-hop, and current stuff; it's the volume thing that bothers me most of the time. There are a few bartenders who are warm and friendly (two females in particular, whose names I can't remember, but one has a great partial sleeve on one arm), but for the most part, the staff (male bartenders in particular) give off a vibe that they really couldn't care less about their customers. Having worked in the industry, this attitude really pisses me off. I couldn't figure out how PYT's employees got away with ignoring their customers on such a regular basis, until the last time I went in, with some out of town guests. As we were settling our tabs (which were much higher than we expected them to be), I happened to glance at the chalkboard behind the bar, which lists the beers and the daily specials. There, in rather small, handwritten print, it said, "20% gratuity added to all bills." Never before had I noticed this "sign," and never before (in my 5 or 6 times there) had a server or bartender informed me of this policy. I'm not even sure if this policy is legal. I mean...sure, we all expect the 18% gratuity added to checks when we go out w/ parties of 6 or more. But three people, sitting at a half-empty bar on a Saturday afternoon, drinking beers and watching the Phils game??? Our bartender said something to the effect of, "Oh, wow. I really didn't think you guys drank that much!" when she gave us our tabs, and asked us to check and make sure she hadn't accidentally charged us twice for anything (since we had two tabs going). Had she not said this, I wouldn't have noticed the 20% gratuity that had been added. So I'm not sure if she was suggesting we look at it, as a way of getting us to stumble upon the automatic gratuity, or if she was genuinely worried she had overcharged us. But the bottom line is, she (and every other server/bartender there) should have just come out and said, "Hey, not sure if you noticed the tiny little chalk-written note on the beer board, but there's an automatic 20% gratuity added to every bill." Naturally, I had already added a 20% tip to my bill (on TOP of the 20% they had already charged), but I hadn't given it back to her yet. So I tossed the first copy into my purse, and recalculated on the 2nd copy. Honestly...I don't know if this is illegal, but it certainly seems unethical, and it's DEFINITELY offensive, especially to a person who tips extremely well on a regular basis. And, honestly, the service at PYT is among the worst I've ever had. They're slow, they're not friendly, and they act like they don't give a sh*t. Which they probably don't, since they get 20% regardless. If you're looking for a laidback time at a bar and you don't care if it takes half an hour to get each of your drinks...give it a try. And try a pickleback shot while you're there. They make their own pickles in-house, and the pickle juice is delicious. But BEWARE of the automatic 20% gratuity.

She never spoke a word during the entire ten minute span I was in there. The problem with these places is that three stars is the best you can reasonably expect. Anything above that is impossible because these wrecker services basically treat their customers like hostages. "We have your car. If you ever want to see it again, bring $300 in unmarked bills to that shady place next to the quarry." They don't advertise because you only need the place when some idiot rear-ends you, and you pick the first one that shows up on Google on your cell phone. So even though I rated it two stars, I don't see how it gets any better. text: I am thrilled to have a nice new Japanese restaurant so close to home! What makes this place special is they appreciate your business and go out of their way to make you feel special! My main dish was the Sushi/sashimi combo ($25.) and the fish was succulent, fresh and melted in my mouth like good sushi should be. It was quality! There were 4 of us and we tried each others dishes. The calamari salad ($13) was fresh as could be with a light batter on the calamari. The best appetizer was the Rock Shrimp Tempura ($12) sweet and spicy and wow...delish! The salmon Teriyaki was excellent! ($18)...it came with fresh veggies an they were done perfectly! The filet Mignon steak ($28) was cooked exactly the way it was asked for! Nice flavor and generous portion. The chicken teriyaki looked like a generous portion ($16)...even had left overs to take home on that dish. Service was over the top great! This tends to be a bit pricey and miso soup or salad is not included in the traditional combo meals, but it is more upscale than most Japanese restaurants and the quality shows! I almost forgot to mention, the chopsticks are not the wooden ones that splinter...they are translucent and quite cool! In fact all of the dishes are trendy and make a nice presentation! Don't forget to BYOB! They will even supply a nice wine bucket for keeping it cold. We were informed the menu will have even more to choose from in July or August. I look forward to trying the Pad Thai as that will be on their new menu! Anyway... Does it get any better? Good service...good food and a bottle of red!!!

text: I'm from Dubai and Toronto, been to some of the finest restaurants in both cities, but I must say that d'Lish is by far one of the best I've been to! On a recent visit to Alberta, escaping my life and the hustle n bustle of To, I decided to visit a friend of mine in Edmonton. The moment I landed I felt like royalty...my friend's gorgous condo which seemed more like a stylish loft/town home, manis and pedis in the afternoon, followed by a faboulous dinner at this lovely restaurant! We were a group of 6, and we started off by wine and some nibbles. Gourmet popcorn...what an ingenious idea!! There were 2 types, truffled oil and maple bacon...i preferred the former but enjoyed the sweetness of the latter..I wish I knew how they did this and I'd have movie nights at home in complete bliss! So now with regards to the food, 4 of us went for the surprise 10 course meal..and boy were we surprised...shocked that it was SOOO d'Lish-ous! We had a wide variety of different textures, flavours, colours..exactly how a meal should me...innovative creations like Shrimp with a sauce in shot glasses, scallops, mushroom crepes, turkey dinner (bread, chutney and turkey balls), beef ribs in mustard sauce...simply DIVINE! all sorts of other goodies too..and portions were terrific! The dessert was tiny, but oh so good..truffled chocolate in some sort of dreamy rasberry coulis sauce garnished with nuts. At that point we didn't mind the smaller dessert as we were so full with everything else. My friend who decided to go with an individual entree had the veggie flatbread pizza...which I tried a little...also baked to perfection. We were thoroughly impressed by the friendly service, the mouth watering food, the elegant decor...maybe I'm in love with this restaurant because I'm not from Edmonton and I know I can't visit it that much (we always want what we can't have!) but I have to say...FABULOUS venue..whether you're on a date, a birthday dinner, or simply dining solo , D'lish is the best choice! text: It has a very interesting decor and is a unique building, so this might be a good place to have a drink, but I'm not sure I would return to dine here. First, let me say that our server was friendly and did his job well. We couldn't ask for much more. Drinks: Several beer choices. They distill their own rum, so we tried a Rum-a-Rita. It has a unique flavor on the back end, which I can only guess was the rum, and was easy to drink. I would definitely recommend these. Appetizers: Trying to decide between Billy Goat Chips & Dip, White Bean & Artichoke Brulee, and Bacon Wrapped Dates ($6.95, see picture), we asked the server for a recommendation. He answered quickly with the dates, and we were not disappointed. These were a unique blend of salty and sweet that worked and came with a nice dipping sauce. Plate of Food: I would not get this. My friend ordered the Plate of Food. She received 2 chili dogs (see picture). Nothing else with it, no sides or veggies, just 2 hot dogs in buns covered in chili, cheese, and bacon bits for $9.95. Not exactly the type of meal most females want for a Saturday night dinner at 7pm for $9.95. Even if they tasted ok, $9.95 is pricey for 2 chili dogs. We happened to arrive just after 2 large tables had ordered and figured the kitchen/chef was so busy with their order, that's why the Plate of Food at the moment was chili dogs, because it was easy to do. Cajun Salmon ($11.95, see picture): The salmon was very good in a tasty sauce with a tiny bit of heat. I can't usually handle spicy, but this was pretty good. The red beans and rice, however, was a whole other story. I took one bite and - what I'm guessing was - the cayenne on the rice was all I could taste for 1/2 the meal. It was soooo spicy hot, I could not touch the rice the rest of the meal. The green beans seemed raw. At first, I thought they were just steamed, but then I tasted the bitterness of the raw bean and noticed they were overly crunchy. I know some people eat green beans raw, but it's just not what I was expecting to come with the salmon.

text: On 5.7.12 I drove 3 hrs to buy a 2008 Toyota Highlander Hybrid Limited from Tri-County. That very evening when I got home I noticed heavy condensation in the driver's side headlight. I figured, ok, warranty issue, so I took it to my local dealer the next day. That afternoon local dealer called to inform me headlight wasn't covered because the left fender had been replaced - car had prior accident damage! This was not disclosed by the dealer and there's nothing on the CARFAX. Note that they knew who owned this vehicle - it was previously used by the local area Toyota Rep!!! Ok, fine, notified dealer and they sent a check to local dealer for repairs. I should also note that the front bumper is not set properly in the front grill or under headlight - so noticeable that there was work done. And why didn't I discover this when I bought the car - because it was cold, overcast and raining - so I didn't notice. Shame on me....NEVER buy a used car in the rain! So anyway, that evening, 5.8.12, got home and noticed that the front windshield was cracked above the rear view mirror - wasn't noticeable before because it was in the black-shaded area on the windshield. Long story short, dealer says is wasn't pre-existing - despite my showing them a picture of a rusted ding on the car frame where something had hit the windshield. Consequently, I filed a complaint with the Better Business Bureau. And now, last night I discovered that the latch to release the driver's side passenger seat does not work. I can't wait to discover what else doesn't work on this car. Thank God I bought the extended warranty. Oh, and this is a "Certified Used Car." Right. So like I said - Buyer Beware. I would not do business with this dealership again (Note that my salesman, Nick, was a decent fellow - I don't think he knew the vehicle had these issues).
