text: So a bunch of my guy friends have been raving nonstop about the lasagna and pizza here so when they invited me to check it out with them, I couldn't say no. The pizzas are a bit expensive, but they are huge, fresh, delicious, and worth it. They will gladly make you a pizza half & half with the variety of toppings offered including artichokes (yum!) and spinach and all the regular meats. I wasn't able to try any of their pastas or other dishes but I've heard great things about them. But, let me tell you, do not come here on an empty stomach expecting to order, get your food, and get out. There is a wait in line and a wait for the food. A long wait in anticipation for the food. A wait so long that every 5 minutes you're second-guessing whether or not they've forgotten your order. You'll play mind tricks on yourself, asking yourself over and over again, "Did she really hear my order? Did I give her my name? Did someone take our pizza? Did those guys come before us or after us? How come they got their food first? Will they run out of dough? Are they closing shop?" That being said, however, they won't forget your order. I was a little concerned at first because we had to repeat our order twice; I almost got the impression that we were bothering her or troubling her by taking our order. But our pizza came out perfectly fine. Although, it took what seemed like an hour before it came out. And they don't forget you. We had been waiting there for a while (it made for a good time of catching up with old friends) and randomly, the lady from behind the counter motioned to my friend. No words, no yelling, just a simple head gesture, beckoning him to come forward. Silence. She hands him a plate of baked dough doused in some olive oil, fresh from the oven. The dough probably comes from leftovers from rolling pizzas, but boy did it whet our appetites. It was deliciously fresh and irresistible. I've always wanted to act in a sitcom, and something about this place reminds me of the Soup Nazi in Seinfeld. Except it's the pizza Nazi. There aren't many wall decorations, just your average cafeteria-style small beginnings. No waiters or waitresses serving you on hand and feet. No one to bus your table for you or refill your Coke. And your regular table conversations will be interrupted by some backstage yelling between the workers or maybe at a customer. You might get a curt or rude word here or there--but it's all part of the experience. Don't come in a rush or with a naive spirit--this is New York Pizza we're talking about...don't expect that Southern hospitality.

Before I found Yelp, I was a Foursquate check-in fiend and I love the fact that you get a free drink with every check-in (and it works for Yelpers too!) and I always went with one of their specialty martinis! They are sweet and unique, my favorite being their cotton candy creation. The menu is a LITTLE overwhelming, they seem to have a lot going on - various themes and what not - but I am a huge advocate for tapas style dining. The food is really good in my opinion and I only had to send something back one time. During my second visit I ordered the chicken skewers and they were ridiculously burnt, to the point where I questioned why they would even bring it out to me in the first place. The waiter apologized, took it away and minutes later brought me a new plate of perfectly cooked chicken and even comped me for it! Now THAT is customer service. The manager came around and chatted us up a bit, but not in the pushy sort of way - which we liked. Our bill was reasonable for the amount of food and drink we ordered, too. text: Who says there's no taste in British food? Oh wait, I said that. The decor here is fantastic, and as an aside, this place is bigger than it looks from the outside. It seems like a vast expanse once you go up the stairs. Anyway, the food here is good. text: This was my first time running the Rock 'n Roll Mardi Gras half marathon. I really enjoyed the experience. The course was nice and flat, except for all the pot holes. The health and fitness expo was huge! I think it has to be the biggest one I've been to for a Rock 'n Roll run (I've done RnR San Jose, RnR Las Vegas and RnR Mardi Gras). I really liked the design for the tech-t. It wasn't the typical boring RnR design they usually have. I wonder if it is because this was the inaugural RnR Mardi Gras run? They had a separate medal design for the half marathoners vs the marathoners. I thought maybe they should have done separate t-shirt colors too, like they did for the inaugural Las Vegas RnR run, but oh well. We purchased the pass for the shuttle ride ($20 for one car, but good for up to four people on the shuttle) to the start from the college which is right next to the park where the run finishes. It was very convenient and well worth it. When we arrived at the start area, they already had booths set up with volunteers handing out water and energy bars! They even had port-o-potties next to each starting corale. Talk about thinking ahead and being organized! It was quite cold in the morning standing around, stretching and waiting for the run to start. It was nice to see that quite a few people wore costumes for the run. Overall it was a great event and they actually had a band that I wanted to stay around to listen to after the run.

text: You know, maybe the food truck thing just isn't for me. Based on the glowing reviews for almost all of them, I must be the only person in Indy who has found a single fault with anything served out of a truck. Either that, or I'm the only one willing to voice it, as most of these places get rave reviews. I don't know how Hitler was able to brainwash millions of people, but I bet it had something to do with food trucks. Byrne's was about the seventh food truck I've tried and the second one serving pizza. I only tried the regular cheese pizza and maybe that was the problem. It just doesn't get more fundamental than that. If the cheese pizza isn't done right, why would I expect anything more complex to be? Personally, I have had better pizza out of the frozen section of the grocery store. Bland and boring. These are just average pies reheated on a gas grill. Oh, and $19 for a large pepperoni pizza? Yikes. Have propane tank refills gotten that expensive? As I mentioned in another recent review, I take pizza seriously. I love it. Remember Pizza the Hutt in the movie Spaceballs? I could run away with him and live happily ever after in greasy bliss. Maybe that's why I am so critical of places like this. I am not comparing Byrne's to other food trucks, I am comparing them to other pizza places. I ask myself if I would drive 10-15 minutes out of my way to eat there if it were a regular stand alone restaurant like I will for other pizza places in town. Definitely not. We have some pretty damn good pizza joints in Indy now and there is no reason for me to forego those in favor of lesser ones.

text: 4.5 stars for SideBern's. It's hard to top the original Bern's in terms of service, food quality and value for what you're getting, and SideBern's wisely doesn't even try. Instead, they opt for a more contemporary fusion menu which rotates out based on the availability of local ingredients. Very similar to the Refinery, except I think SB nails the ambiance a lot better. We spent two hours at the restaurant during our dining experience and it was a very comfortable place to do it. This was an anniversary dinner for my wife and I, so I tried to make it a little more special by ordering a bottle of champagne when I made the reservations. The staff on the phone was very accommodating with helping me pick out a good choice. Be prepared for a little sticker shock even for aged liquor, but I assure you it's well worth it. Their beer selection is also very impressive and looks as if the selections were hand picked to go along with the food being presented. The rest of the wait staff were very friendly and even stopped by our table to wish us a happy anniversary. Even better than booze, they also have an entire vegetarian menu which rotates out along with their normal menu. They don't scale back on it at all either, so there are plenty of choices. My wife and I went with the $55per person tasting, which consisted of 6 courses and a little pre-appetizer course. Since there was so much food flying around I won't fill up this review with every little dish, but suffice to say there was ample variety. Highlights include an almond vichysoise with goat cheese which left us aching for more, oregano scened tofu with some amazing chick pea puree that I will never be able to duplicate, polenta that gives mac and cheese a run for its money with wild mushrooms, and a macadamia nut bread pudding that somehow filled the remaining gaps left in my stomach. To me, SideBerns is the epitome of a good romantic restaurant. While food plays a central role, it's really about the whole experience. The wait staff are just there to aid and facilitate conversation between you and your loved one. The food, just another topic of conversation and something you get to share. And the champagne is there to make you seem just the slightest bit more insightful and witty. I don't say any of that to devalue the food, staff, or decor, but to pay it a very high compliment. Check it out for your next special occasion!

text: If Occupy Philly had a sponsor, I like to think Underdogs would be it. It's a place where revolutionary spirit drapes the walls with its raised, clenched fist mural; the kind of artwork that would be welcoming to a group that, say, might want to overthrow the Fed and return to the gold standard. But as far as I can tell, Underdogs is less concerned with Ben Bernanke and more focused on putting out great hot dogs. The buns are not the flimsy 4th of July cookout ones you snag off a grocery store shelf. Sturdy, crackly sides are just dense and chewy enough to make you appreciate the quality rolls without any unnecessary padding. A proper meat/toppings to bread ratio is paramount and they've got it down. The Special ($3.50), with pepper hash and russian dressing, probably pairs nicely with 6-8 lagers and is a late night craving waiting to happen. The Chihuahua ($4.50) was my only foray into the sausages and the queso blanco adds a nice, needed smooth finish to play against the sharp spices of chorizo. The salty peanut taste of the My Thai ($4) dog marries well with the cool, crispy papaya slaw, but I only want peanut sauce with chicken and some kind of noodle. The fries ($2.25/reg) stand up on their own merit. Unless a better writer shows up to finish this review I'll lazily tell you to think of Five Guys fries, greasy paper bag and all. But stay away from the ketchup when you peel back your greasy bag of spuds. Utah sauce is another weird cult-ish thing to come out of Utah, but this one is actually worth following blindly. Ketchup, mayo, and pickle juice--stop, get that look off your face--forms a surprisingly addicting condiment. It's a fairly smooth concoction before the pickle juice kicks your palate with just a bit of brine. There was nothing wrong with the chocolate cayenne mole--nice heat and all--I just didn't think it matched up well with the spuds. When the rack I purchased from them did not fit well with the panniers I purchased from them, the owner Mike McGettigan -- the friendliest bike geek you'll meet this side of David Byrne -- simply agreed to replace it with another model at no cost for parts or labor. When I came in to pick up my bike from a tune-up and head out for the day, but realized I forgot to bring my lock, Mike lent me one for a couple days. While I can't speak to day-to-day issues, if you are into cross or touring bikes, Trophy is the best shop in the city. Mike is also active in the local cycling advocacy community, so doubleplus bonus points.

text: I think I might have found my FAVORITE frozen yogurt place in St. Louis. And after trying every single self-serve froyo place here, I can say that with complete confidence. Actually, now that I think about it, it's quite embarrassing that I've been to every froyo place in STL. I'm not proud. Moving on. I went to Yogurtland for lunch (froyo is the lunch of champions, dontcha know?). It's in Kirkwood in a little strip plaza next to Five Guys. The place itself is super cute, and has a Sanyo sort of theme about it. I walked in, and the friendly girl working the counter welcomed me and immediately gave me a handful of sample cups. Okay, now this is my kinda place. Yogurtland has quite possibly the best (and most creative) froyo flavors I've encountered so far. I sampled: Strawberry NY cheesecake Caramel almond Double cookies and cream Chocolate milkshake Vanilla wafer Original tart Each one was special and delicious in its own way. But Red Mango's original tart beats Yogurtland's original tart. Valiant try by Yogurtland, however! Another awesome thing about Yogurtland? THE TOPPINGS! By far, the best selection of toppings I've encountered (Yogoluv is a close second). Each topping is clearly marked and labeled. They even have lychee here! I wasn't brave enough to try it; it looked really...interesting, to say the least. I settled with the Vanilla Wafer flavored froyo (seriously amazing!) topped with cheesecake bites and ghiradelli chocolate chips. I'm not sure how much Yogurtland charges per ounce, but it seemed really cheap -- my full cup of froyo plus toppings was a little over 3 bucks. Nice! I have a feeling that many more of my lunch breaks will be spent at Yogurtland. YUM.

text: When I created my Yelp profile, I had a simple philosophy of writing reviews - Write about food that is great tasting, authentic, healthy, and has a class. Looking at it's ratings distribution, Pam's have received seven five stars, seventeen four stars, five three stars, and only three one stars, which overall gives Four Star Rating to this place, and when the populace looks at the rating, they assume this is a great place and probably enjoy the food too. When Chris Powell and others are trying to reshape the nation into more psychical fit society, we have Pam's and similar establishments across the country serving up battered, fried, dusted with powered sugar, and with a side of cherry sauce Twinkies to indulge excessive amount of free calories into our diets. Ron Swanson, a lovable character played by Nick Offerman on NBC's hit show "Parks and Recreation," said it well; "If you want to eat garbage, balloon up to 600 pounds and die of a heart attack at 43, you can. text: I visited Saudia's July 21, 2012. I took a friend here because we wanted "Soul Food" and the person had already tried "another" establishment in the past. Now, I did call ahead to ask if there was a sitting area and was informed they have a couple tables - and thats exactly what they have. This location is not for you to take a friend to sit and eat and chat. I mean, that's what we did, because we were from out of town (NYC) but basically this place is best for take-out only. Now, on to the food. I must say, I investigated a bit before visiting, so I was looking forward to the Cuban Turkey Wings, but they we all out when I arrived. So I had the smothered turkey wings with mac & cheese and yams. The wings were very well seasoned and fall-off-the-bone tender. The gravy was alright, it could have used a bit more salt or seasoning. But you could tell the wings were marinated or something because the meat was seasoned all the way through. Yams were nice and sweet, even a little gooey - yum. And the mac & cheese....Let me say this. I LOVE cheese, and LOVE mac & cheese just as much, so I'm very critical. This mac & chesse was great. It was different, with some extra seasoning you don't typically find in southern mac & cheese; something with herbs because I saw the green specks. High levels of yumminess! I will caution you: if you are diabetic, you'd better stay away from that orange drink - you've been warned!!! Its very good, but VERY sweet. And the melted ice doesn't even dilute it so that should be a sign. Overall, the food was good. Like I said, this location is best for take out and I would have loved to try some other dishes but they were finished. Definitely a place to try out!

text: We stayed here opening weekend and have stayed a couple more times in the six months since. Overall, this is a nice hotel. It really feels more like a typical nice convention hotel to me (which it is) than a luxury hotel. It just does not have the touches to put it in the latter category for me. The service here, however, is on par with any hotel in the city. It is top notch. Anything you need, they are happy to help. The restaurants are a decent option but I'll do individual reviews for those. The rooms are a decent size but not as big as those in other JWs. They are clean and comfortable. I think the bathroom is small for a hotel of this caliber. They had to cram a thousand rooms in this joint, though, so maybe that's part of the reason. They have an indoor pool and hot tub. These are nice options, especially in the winter, but this is another area I thought could have been bigger. The fitness facility on the other hand is huge. My wife travels a lot for work and we are loyal Marriott customers so one of our favorite activities is comparing the concierge/executive lounges at the various properties. The lounge here is pretty damn nice. They also serve food on the weekends which is very rare, as these hotels tend to cater to the Monday-Thursday business crowd. I will certainly recommend this hotel to friends and family coming in from out of town. Because they do have so many rooms, rates are very reasonable when there is not a large event in town.

text: People like me and other New Orleanians are so lucky to have Louisiana Running Company! These guys are awesome, very friendly, really know running, and give lots back to the community. The owners, Pat and Jen, are both runners and really get it. They are not salesman, they are peers and runners. They absolutely care about your running and enjoy seeing people enjoy running. The service here is way better than any running store in NOLA and the prices at the store are completely fair. Everyone here is friendly and just nice. They carry a different selection of shoes than other stores do and what they carry is really good. Unlike some stores, they actually analyze your gait before making a quick recommendation. I don't see how you can recommend stuff without watching people run. They're sure to put you in the right stuff and do what they do very well. As a runner who's had less than stellar experiences at other stores in NOLA, I can for sure say that this is the best running store. It's just above and beyond. The final great part (aside from everything else), though, is their focus on the running community. These guys are at like every local race and have great run groups and community activities. We have eaten at other bubba gump locations before and have always been satisfied, but this was very disappointing. text: Burgers, craft beer and a diverse whiskey list sound great on paper and I expected to be blown away. I found that while the tap list is worth coming back for, the overall experience left something to be desired. I was helped by 5+ people during the duration of my dinner. Different people were taking orders, delivering food, getting drinks, etc. and it resulted in a rushed feel. They are extremely over-staffed from the looks of it and I know they just opened, so this isn't too big of a deal, but something to note. I ordered bruschetta as an appetizer and it was pretty good, though nothing outstanding. I would order it again. The fig marmelade burger was decent, though it seemed to add up to less than I was hoping for. The sweet potato fries were a definite letdown; way too sweet, and the cinnamon sprinkled on top doesn't help matters out. The food all has a hint of being from a chain - the produce isn't as fresh tasting as that from other similar restaurants around town and everything tastes very 'safe'. Anyways, the overall aesthetic of the restaurant is good but the experience was underwhelming. I would come back but not before Pace Food + Drink or Union Ale. I'll probably sit at the bar next time for drinks.
label: NEG
